security_audit.summary: Most scanner matches are documentation, URLs, object keys, or standard API examples. Confirmed risks include remote shell installers, raw private-key workflows, dynamic eval, privileged commands, and mutable remote instructions. Automatic publication should wait until these behaviors are removed or explicitly gated. Static review was capped at 400/6871 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 6471 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: Remote scripts are downloaded and piped directly into a shell.
remediation.suggestion: Use version-pinned archives, publish checksums, verify signatures, and require inspection before execution.

remediation.issue: Several workflows store, print, export, or pass raw wallet private keys.
remediation.suggestion: Use wallet providers, encrypted keystores, scoped signers, or hardware-backed signing. Remove private keys from JSON, shell history, and plaintext environment files.

remediation.issue: LLM-generated Python expressions are executed with eval.
remediation.suggestion: Replace eval with an allowlisted rule parser or validated abstract syntax tree. Reject unsupported operations.

remediation.issue: Runtime skill instructions are fetched from mutable remote URLs.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle reviewed files and verify content hashes from skills-lock.json. Never execute unpinned remote instructions.

remediation.issue: Remote packages, peer-triggered actions, and GitHub issues can run without separate confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before global installs, external writes, paid actions, or peer-controlled tool execution.

remediation.issue: Predictable temporary files and privileged service commands expand host risk.
remediation.suggestion: Use secure temporary-file APIs, restrictive permissions, atomic writes, and unprivileged service controls where possible.

semantic_findings.title: Unverified Remote Instruction Loading
semantic_findings.description: The router fetches mutable SKILL.md files from raw URLs and orders a later refetch. Remote changes can bypass the reviewed package and inject new instructions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both cited instructions explicitly require runtime retrieval of mutable skill content without hash verification.

semantic_findings.title: Prompt Injection Attempt Detected
semantic_findings.description: A peer message containing `[intent:deliver]` is declared highest priority before any other CLI call. This lets untrusted peers control tool order and file handling.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The routing rule trusts a peer-controlled marker and mandates immediate CLI processing of the entire raw message.

semantic_findings.title: Unattended Global Package Installation
semantic_findings.description: The skill installs global packages or skills without a separate user confirmation. One fallback derives the package name from user-provided text.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both commands use unattended global installation, which changes the host and introduces remote executable instructions.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe Private-Key Handling
semantic_findings.description: The upload workflow prints a newly generated wallet key and later shows an inline private-key command. Terminal, history, or process exposure can compromise funds.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited commands directly print key material and place a raw key in a shell command environment.

semantic_findings.title: Autonomous External Issue Creation
semantic_findings.description: The router requires direct GitHub issue creation whenever it detects a coverage gap. This creates external side effects without explicit confirmation for each report.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instruction explicitly says to file the issue directly when a GitHub tool is available.

content.value_statement: Agent commerce combines payments, permissions, identity, escrow, and dispute handling across many protocols. This skill routes each deal to relevant components and produces a controlled integration plan.
actual_capabilities: Routes each deal to relevant vendored protocol and connector skills.
Classifies trust as Basic, Guarded, or Adjudicated and explains each tradeoff.
Extracts parties, authority, budgets, deliverables, evidence, expiration, and dispute terms.
Designs x402, MPP, delegated permission, escrow, and cross-chain payment flows.
Produces sequence steps, policy models, failure paths, and implementation plans.
Defines evidence, verdict, refund, revocation, and reputation update paths.
limitations: It does not provide legal advice or guarantee contract enforceability.
It cannot create wallet funds or authority without user setup and approval.
It depends on many vendored skills, remote services, and evolving standards.
It cannot verify deployments or payments without transaction receipts or signed evidence.

use_cases.title: Plan a paid agent API
use_cases.description: Select payment, permission, evidence, and refund components for a paid service integration.

use_cases.title: Limit delegated spending
use_cases.description: Define caps, allowed targets, expiration, revocation, and monitoring for an autonomous agent.

use_cases.title: Structure a disputed service deal
use_cases.description: Combine escrow, delivery evidence, review criteria, and settlement outcomes before work begins.

prompt_templates.title: Compare trust levels
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain Basic, Guarded, and Adjudicated options for this deal: [deal]. Recommend one level and list the missing facts.

prompt_templates.title: Design a guarded payment
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a testnet x402 flow for [service]. Add a weekly budget, per-request cap, approved payee, expiration, and revocation path.

prompt_templates.title: Create an adjudicated escrow
prompt_templates.prompt: Structure an escrowed deal for [deliverable]. Define evidence, review criteria, dispute triggers, release conditions, refund conditions, and finality.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an agent-commerce architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this architecture: [architecture]. Identify unbounded authority, chain mismatches, missing receipts, unsafe custody, weak evidence, and incomplete dispute enforcement.

output_examples.input: A research agent needs five paid reports each week from one approved provider.
output_examples.output: Guarded design: bounded weekly and per-request spending, one approved payee, seven-day expiration, signed receipts, and manual revocation.

output_examples.input: A contractor receives payment only after an independent reviewer accepts the deliverable.
output_examples.output: Adjudicated escrow: lock funds, define evidence and review criteria, allow a dispute window, then release or refund from the verdict.

output_examples.input: An agent must use a service on another chain without unlimited token approvals.
output_examples.output: Cross-chain plan: confirm source and destination chains, select a value route, cap approvals, simulate first, and require receipts before continuing.

best_practices: Start with discovery and state what funds, permissions, and evidence are currently available.
Use testnets, small balances, narrow allowlists, short expirations, and explicit revocation.
Require transaction hashes, signed artifacts, or receipts before reporting completion.
anti_patterns: Do not request private keys, seed phrases, or unrestricted bearer wallet files.
Do not treat a payment rail as escrow, refund protection, or dispute resolution.
Do not run remote installers or global package installs without explicit review and confirmation.

faq.question: Does this skill move funds automatically?
faq.answer: No. It designs and routes flows, while wallet approval and available authority remain user controlled.

faq.question: Can it choose between x402 and MPP?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses x402 for paid requests and MPP for metered or streaming payment sessions.

faq.question: Does it provide legal advice?
faq.answer: No. It structures technical obligations and dispute workflows but does not determine legal enforceability.

faq.question: Can it design revocable agent permissions?
faq.answer: Yes. It can specify bounded authority, caveats, expiration, monitoring, and verdict-driven revocation paths.

faq.question: How does it confirm a deployment or payment?
faq.answer: It requires a transaction hash, receipt, signed artifact, deployed address, or equivalent proof.

faq.question: Is production deployment recommended first?
faq.answer: No. The skill recommends testnet simulation, small limits, and explicit user approval before production use.
